subject: Implementation: Cost/perf tuning plan for CourierAI onboarding
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@courierai.com>, Alex Park <alex@courierai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation: Cost/perf tuning plan for CourierAI onboarding

Hi Priya / Alex —

Great to be kicking off implementation next week. To keep the pilot tight and predictable, I put together a compact plan focused on the three knobs we recommended: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profile selection — plus routing fallbacks for peak traffic. Attached is a one‑page Redwood tuning checklist and an example prefix distribution CSV (I omitted any PII).

Proposed next steps: 
- 60‑minute tuning workshop (engineering + CS + your infra team) — agenda: workload profile, SLOs, fallback policy.
- We’ll ask you to share a 48‑hour sample of request metadata (prefix lengths, avg tokens, peak RPS) — CSV is fine.
- Post‑workshop: Redwood delivers a recommended config (batching window, kv cache policy, recommended quant profiles for your mix) and a canary roll plan.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the sample data? I put Marissa and Karthik on the thread for scheduling and the technical deep dive.

Thanks,
— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555‑0192

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@courierai.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation: Cost/perf tuning plan for CourierAI onboarding

Thanks, Soojin — this looks good. We can get you a 48‑hour trace from our staging tier. I’ll own gathering the sample and anonymizing any user IDs; Alex will help with retention windows. Couple of quick questions before the workshop: 

1) Do you support lower‑precision INT8 or per‑layer quant profiles for the small models? We want to understand quality tradeoffs.
2) For routing fallbacks: can Redwood configure a policy that prefers cheaper variants during non‑peak windows but forces high‑quality variants for latency‑sensitive routes?

We prefer the workshop on Wed 14 Oct after 11am PT if that works. Also, we have a procurement SOW that needs a minor update; I’ll attach SOW_v2.

— Priya
Priya Singh
Head of Platform Engineering | CourierAI
priya.singh@courierai.com | +1 (617) 555‑0123

Attachments: SOW_CourierAI_v2.docx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@courierai.com>, Alex Park <alex@courierai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation: Cost/perf tuning plan for CourierAI onboarding

Perfect — Wed 14 Oct after 11am PT works for us. We’ll schedule a 60‑minute slot and share the agenda in advance. Quick answers: 

1) Quantization: Redwood supports multiple quantization profiles. For the small models we recommend starting with dynamic FP16 -> static INT8 for non‑sensitive routes; Karthik will include an example quality checklist you can run locally (perplexity + a small holds set). Per‑layer tuning is possible but usually reserved after the canary phase because it requires longer validation.

2) Routing policies: yes. Redwood can express time‑based and route‑based policies. Typical pattern we use for customers: 
   - Primary: high‑quality FP16/FP32 variant for checkout/critical flows (low latency SLO).
   - Secondary: quantized INT8 variant for bulk/async requests.
   - Hours‑of‑day policy: allow fallback to cheaper variant outside 9am‑6pm business window.

For the workshop, please include a short sample of: 
- Top 50 prefixes by request count (CSV) — your courier routes are a great example.
- Typical session lengths (avg tokens) and 95th percentile.
- Any hard latency SLOs (p95 target).

Marissa will send a calendar invite and Karthik will lead the kernel/quant conversation.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@courierai.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation: Cost/perf tuning plan for CourierAI onboarding

Hi Priya — quick technical note to prep the workshop: 

If you can provide the prefix distribution we can prototype batching and cache hit rates quickly. A couple of pointers for the CSV schema that speed the analysis: 
- prefix, count, avg_tokens, p95_tokens, route_tag
- include a boolean column for latency‑sensitive routes (true/false) so we can prioritize those for FP32/FP16.

On quantization: for your use case (many short inference calls tied to status updates), batching provides the largest win on cost without touching quantization; my plan for the workshop: show a short matrix of batch_size x avg_latency impact, then demonstrate an INT8 profile for low‑sensitivity routes.

Also: we can pre‑stage a canary with 10% traffic routed to an INT8 variant and collect quality metrics for 2 business days before wider rollout. If you have a small labeled set (10–20 critical prompts) include that — it speeds evaluation.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@courierai.com>

Thanks everyone — I’ve attached the 48‑hour anonymized sample and a tiny holdout set (10 prompts) for quality evals. We reviewed the SOW edits and are happy to sign once we lock the canary window. Calendar invite accepted for Wed 14 Oct 11:30am PT. Looking forward to the workshop.

Artifacts attached: courier_prefix_distribution.csv, holdout_prompts.txt, SOW_CourierAI_v2.docx

Best,
— Priya
